issues.failure_explanation: For the data F=x_1x_2, constraints x_1<=0, x_2<=-|theta|, the minimizer set at theta!=0 is {(0,x_2): x_2<=-|theta|} and at theta=0 it is {x_1<=0,x_2=0} U {x_1=0,x_2<=0}; both are unbounded, so Assumption ass:specialcase(iii)/ass:standing(iii) (bounded, locally bounded solution sets) fails although the section declares the assumptions to hold throughout. Consequently the example does not witness strictness of the inclusion eq:clarkesubdiffvf, which is stated under Assumptions ass:standing, and the set of all adjoint outputs at theta=0 contains every u in [x_1,-x_1] for x*=(x_1,0), x_1<0, i.e. all of R, so D_f is not locally bounded and is not a conservative field, contrary to the intro's framing of this example. (The example also says m=1 while G has three components.)

issues.failure_explanation: The only conditions imposed on the radii are r_k>0, r_k->0 and pairwise disjointness of the balls. Under these conditions alone (a) the balls may intersect C, so ḡ(z)=0 on C can fail since the bump terms are nonnegative and positive inside the balls; and (b) even with r_k < dist(z_k,C), differentiability at z̄ in C fails when r_k is comparable to dist(z_k,C): taking z_k -> z̄ with r_k = dist(z_k,C)/2 and h pointing from z̄ to z_k with ||h|| = ||z̄-z_k|| - r_k/2 ≈ 1.5 r_k gives ḡ(z̄+h) - ḡ(z̄) >= phi(1/2) r_k ≈ (2/3)phi(1/2)||h||, which is not o(||h||). Differentiability requires r_k = o(dist(z_k,C)) (e.g. r_k <= dist(z_k,C)^2), which is neither imposed nor argued; the proof merely asserts differentiability.

\(C\) is the zero of an infinitely differentiable and non-negative function \(\bar{f}\colon \Rell \to \R\) and, for any \(z \in C\), \(\nabla \bar{f}(z) = 0\).

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the adjoint formula (form:asm) itself may fail for a differentiable objective without definability. What Claim theo:counterex establishes is that the set-valued map D_f built from the Clarke subdifferential of F is not conservative. In the example, F is differentiable, attains its minimum 0 on C, so ∇F=0 on C, and the constraint is inactive at minimizers (λ=0); hence the actual adjoint output ∇_θ L(x*,λ*,θ) = ∇_θ F(x*,θ) = 0 = f'(θ) on (0,1). The failure is due to replacing ∇F by the (large) Clarke subdifferential, not to the adjoint formula with the pointwise gradient.

failure_location.quote: Indeed, in the absence of definability, the adjoint formula may fail to carry variational meaning for the value function, even for locally Lipschitz, path differentiable and (point-wise) differentiable objective function with smooth constraints.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the intro/abstract/Section 4.4 statements to say that, without definability, the Clarke-based (or any closed-graph conservative-field-based) adjoint set D_f of Theorem theo:main need not be conservative, rather than that the adjoint formula itself loses variational meaning.
issues.overall_effect: The scope claim 'the adjoint formula fails even for differentiable objectives without definability' is not supported; only the Clarke-based conservative-field construction D_f is shown to fail.
issues.title: Prose overstates the counterexample: the adjoint formula with the true gradient of the differentiable objective is correct there
issues.why_classification: Only the wording of the scope statement must be adjusted; the formal counterexample and all theorems are unaffected.
